newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money eases back as reserves grow.
newsitem.headline: German call money eases back as reserves grow.

text.p: German call money rates were softer on Thursday with the market enjoying healthy reserves.
Traders said the rates started the session at around 3.08 to 3.10 percent, and eased off slightly more towards midday.

"Things are looking a bit softer now," said one money market trader at a Swiss bank in Frankfurt. "We have seen more offers than bids during the morning, and rates have come down to around 3.05 to 3.08 percent."
Smooth liquidity was the main factor behind the easing, players said, with reserves held by banks up to 42.3 billion marks on Wednesday from 41.7 billion on Tuesday.
"We have some good reserve figures at the moment and the market is happy with liquidity levels," the trader said. "I expect this situation will continue for the next two or three sessions."
Another trader said that large banks would build up reserves on any offers under 3.10 percent, preventing any significant retreat in call money rates.
Banks' average holdings totalled 41.1 billion marks on Wednesday, up slightly from 41.0 in the previous session.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average (FIONA) stood at 3.11000 percent on Thursday, down from 3.12400 on Wednesday.
